audit_target.author: deepseek-v4-pro/T748
audit_target.audited_at: HEAD 2ec4f93 (spec.md unmodified vs its own pin)

findings.finding: ORC-CTRL-1 claims "Every id in §1–§7 has at least one arm here; the seed's named controls are the mandatory core" (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S06-orchestration-refactor/spec.md:454-456). Counted against §9's own table's "flips" column (spec.md:457-472): §1–§7 carry 31 normative ORC-* ids (GOAL-1..4, POL-1..7, PAUSE-1..3, DASH-1..5, ARB-1..4, REG-1..4, GATE-1/2, ORIENT-1, PROV-1). The flips column names exactly 15 distinct ids (ARB-1, ARB-2, ARB-3, DASH-2, DASH-3, DASH-5, PAUSE-1, PAUSE-2, POL-2, POL-7, PROV-1, REG-1, REG-2, REG-3, REG-4). 16 of 31 have no arm at all: GOAL-1..4, POL-1, POL-3, POL-4, POL-5, POL-6, PAUSE-3, DASH-1, DASH-4, ARB-4, GATE-1, GATE-2, ORIENT-1 — including load-bearing ids such as POL-3 (the appetite dial's 0-9 semantics), POL-4/GATE-2 (the merged cooldown state machine, this sprint's own headline feature), DASH-4 (the one-pane worked example the acceptance bar is measured against), and ARB-4 (the kernel-attested-identity security Must carried from §7c.18). Section 0's own rule states plainly: "an id with no control is not a requirement, it is a wish." By that rule, roughly half this spec's own normative statements are wishes, and ORC-CTRL-1's universal-coverage sentence is exactly the un-audited green reading this project's standing doctrine (never trust a green [control set]) forbids — the same overclaim pattern found in the S04 spec audit (findings/T584-s04-spec-audit.json finding 1).
findings.disposition: Rev before ratification: either add arms for the uncovered ids (minimum: POL-3 appetite-dial bounds, POL-4/GATE-2 the merged cooldown machine's own state transitions, DASH-4 the whole-pane composition, ARB-4 kernel-vs-env identity spoof) or restate ORC-CTRL-1 as "C1–C14 are the mandatory core; the remaining N ids are owed arms in P3" and enumerate them by id. An unenumerated remainder is how coverage debt goes silent, and this spec's own §0 names that exact failure mode.

findings.finding: §0 states the migration surface is "counted, not asserted": "5 named tools + 75 tools/regression-*.sh scripts at HEAD" and explicitly names the one delta it accounts for (regression-window-resilience.sh, T736 at 11b69b8), closing with "a script left uncounted is a silent truncation and a spec defect" (spec.md:52-55). §8's disposition table sums 17 ABSORB + 14 REWIRE + 44 SURVIVE = 75 (spec.md:412, verified by re-adding the three sub-lists — each sums correctly). But `ls tools/regression-*.sh | wc -l` at the current HEAD (2ec4f93) returns 76, not 75. The uncounted script is tools/regression-directive-id-uniqueness.sh, added at be87b34 ("T758: directive-ID mint from ledger max + append uniqueness backstop", 2026-08-23 14:15:31) — 71 minutes AFTER the spec's own citation pin a1415fe (13:04:59) — and it appears in none of the ABSORB/REWIRE/SURVIVE lists. This is precisely the failure mode ORC-PLAN-5 (spec.md:445-447) names: "a script left off the table is a spec defect, not a reader's problem." By the spec's own rule, ratifying at 75 now understates the true count by one.
findings.disposition: Amend §8's table to 76, adding tools/regression-directive-id-uniqueness.sh. Its natural home is ABSORB alongside regression-directive-integrity.sh and regression-directive-kill.sh in P4.1 (policy reader / expiring pauses) — it tests directive-ID minting, the same subsystem T758 just touched and the same phase those two siblings already occupy. Re-pin the citation to the current HEAD or explicitly note the pin is intentionally stale pending this amendment.

findings.finding: The spec contradicts its own amendment. §2's "Amendment 2026-08-23 (T766)" (spec.md:182-186) states the window_budgets block "is retired" — "regulation collapses to APPETITE (steering) + COOLDOWN (reactive)" — and this is independently verified: T766 (cf7fc68, 2026-08-23 15:09:01, after the spec's a1415fe pin at 13:04:59) deleted window_policy.py's token_meter/budget_for/estimate_lane_tokens/meter_level/budget_check/effective_cap/record_budget_override functions wholesale. Yet three later sections of the SAME document still bake the retired meter in as normative: (a) ORC-DASH-4's worked-example pane (spec.md:244, :254-255) lists "window budget + appetite" as one of the five dashboard sections and renders a live "budget/5h" column populated with "35.0M" for the claude family — the exact T736 number the amendment says is superseded; (b) ORC-DASH-5 (spec.md:268) names the window+appetite section's data source as "policy file `window_budgets` + `appetite`" — citing the block-name the amendment retired two sections earlier; (c) ORC-ACC-1's third acceptance bar (spec.md:496) requires the one pane to show "per-family window budget and appetite", making a retired mechanism part of the ratification gate itself.
findings.disposition: Reconcile §4 and §10 with the §2 amendment before ratification: drop the budget/5h column from ORC-DASH-4's pane and its worked numbers, restate ORC-DASH-5's data source as appetite + the §6 cooldown machine's runtime state only, and reword ORC-ACC-1(3) to "per-family appetite and cap" (dropping "window budget"). Leaving this uncorrected means a builder implementing the acceptance bar literally re-introduces the meter the sprint just killed.

findings.finding: oxalpha's appetite classification changed from RESERVED to SPEND by a same-day operator ruling that landed AFTER the spec's citation pin, and the spec's worked examples still encode the old value. Commit 2ec4f93 (2026-08-23 16:45:07, "oxalpha appetite reserved->spend (operator: free during blind test)", also recorded in docs/status/landmark-waypoints-seed-2026-08-23.md §5: "free while the blind test runs; test and compare it at every reasonable opportunity; never penalize it on speed") postdates a1415fe (13:04:59) by over 3 hours. But: ORC-POL-5's worked JSON (spec.md:152) still carries `{"model": "oxalpha", "dial": -1, ... "reason": "RESERVED — identity sealed, never auto-drawn"}`; ORC-POL-6 (spec.md:188-194) builds its entire rationale — and one of the two [design-open] items in §12 (spec.md:550) — on oxalpha being the RESERVED sentinel's sole real-world subject; ORC-DASH-4's pane (spec.md:259) renders `oxalpha — — RESERVED — (identity sealed)`. All three are now stale. This also moots the §12 design-open question itself: if oxalpha (the only entry ever carrying RESERVED) is now SPEND, there is no live subject left for the "-1 sentinel vs explicit RESERVED string" choice to apply to, and design would be choosing an encoding for a category the policy file no longer populates.
findings.disposition: Amend ORC-POL-5's oxalpha row to an appetite dial consistent with SPEND (operator-set value, owner citing the 2ec4f93 ruling), rewrite ORC-POL-6 to state RESERVED is not currently in use rather than describing oxalpha as its exemplar, update ORC-DASH-4's oxalpha row to show a real dial/cap instead of the RESERVED placeholder, and either drop §12's RESERVED-encoding design-open item or explicitly reframe it as speculative (no current consumer) so design doesn't spend a cycle on a moot choice.

findings.finding: Checked but NOT a contradiction, contrary to what the audit brief suggested checking for: T772's ratified operator direction ("cost is REMOVED from model choice entirely", untracked/T772-cost-ladder-quality-gate.md §Ratified direction) governs `soloPick` / task-to-model assignment in src/managent/main.zig — a different subsystem from this spec's policy file, which governs per-family/per-model appetite, caps, allow/deny, and cooldowns (fan-out and back-pressure, not task assignment). Grep for "cost" across the spec (3 hits: spec.md:109, 359, 575) turns up only the D036/T736 invisible-default kill and the T732 "onboarding costs one registry entry" figure — no cost-based selection logic is described anywhere in this document. T772 therefore invalidates nothing here; it is a live tension in a sibling subsystem (assign/soloPick), not this spec.
findings.disposition: No amendment required for this item. Worth one sentence in the spec's cross-reference list noting the two subsystems are distinct, so a future reader doesn't assume this spec already resolves T772's finding.

findings.finding: ORC-GOAL-2's migration-scope table (spec.md:72-80) states window_policy.py is "737" lines at HEAD. Current line count (post-T766, which the spec's own §2 amendment already accounts for) is 548 — `wc -l tools/window_policy.py`. The table's per-file line counts, and the "3479 lines" sum they roll up to (spec.md:81), are pinned to the seed-time snapshot and were not recomputed after T766 landed, even though the spec text elsewhere (the Amendment) is aware T766 happened.
findings.disposition: Recompute the ORC-GOAL-2 table's line counts (and the 3479 total) against the current HEAD, or explicitly footnote that the counts are pinned to a1415fe and are known-stale by the amount T766 already removed. This is a much smaller instance of finding 3's underlying problem: the document knows about T766 in one place and not in every place it should.

findings.finding: ORC-REG-1 (spec.md:304-309) says agent-authored bundle filenames "collide gracefully" with no stated resolution. Two readings a builder could pick between: (a) the second writer's `add` auto-suffixes and both bundles register under distinct task IDs, or (b) the second writer is refused and must rename. These have materially different UX and failure modes (silent auto-rename vs. hard stop), and nothing in §6 states which.
findings.disposition: One sentence in ORC-REG-1 or ORC-REG-3 naming the resolution (recommend: refuse with a named alternative filename, consistent with ORC-REG-3's "never a lecture, always a worked example" convention) — this is exactly the T759 "no two readings" class of ambiguity the brief asked to check for.

findings.finding: ORC-DASH-4's worked pane (spec.md:249-263) renders "appetite" as a per-FAMILY word (SPEND / OFF / PROBE / RESERVED), while ORC-POL-3 (spec.md:120-124) defines appetite as a per-MODEL 0-9 dial ("family setting is bulk convenience"). No rule anywhere states how a family's several per-model dials roll up into one categorical word for display — two builders implementing the dashboard from this spec alone could invent different rollup rules (e.g. min of the family's dials vs. a separate family-level override entry) and both would satisfy the text.
findings.disposition: ORC-DASH-4 or ORC-DASH-5 should state the derivation explicitly (e.g. "a family's displayed word is derived from a stated function of its member dials — recommend design specify a single deterministic mapping, e.g. floor thresholds") and mark it `[design-open]` if the mapping itself is genuinely undecided, rather than leaving it implicit in a worked example.

notes:
T778 — independent, first-read audit of the S06 orchestration-refactor spec (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S06-orchestration-refactor/spec.md rev 1, authored deepseek-v4-pro/T748). Non-deepseek auditor per the measurement methodology's independence gate. No writes to the spec or any source file; only findings/T778-s06-spec-audit.json and findings/T778-context.json written. Inbox polled at claim and before reporting done — empty both times, no directive IDs to record.

WHAT PASSES. The spec's structure and self-discipline are genuinely strong: normative ids are systematically assigned, the [design-open] convention is used correctly and both instances found (reconciler fold-point, RESERVED encoding) state real options with a stated recommendation rather than hand-waving, the §11 traceability table maps every one of the seed's 8 rulings plus the named feedstock/ruling citations to a spec home with no ruling silently dropped (verified line-by-line against docs/status/orchestration-refactor-seed-2026-08-23.md — no weakening found: ORC-PAUSE-1's 5-hour default and loud-lapse language matches the seed verbatim in substance, ORC-DASH-2/3's short-names-only and empty-section-omission rules match, ORC-ARB-1's T712/T713 absorption and T711 prerequisite match, ORC-REG-3's 4 seed-stated fields plus its 5th field (gate declaration) is legitimately imported from the separately-ratified §7c.21, not fabricated, and is itself separately traced in §11's bottom row). The T732 baseline numbers cited in ORC-PROV-1/ORC-CTRL-4 ("4 tracked files, 65 insertions/5 deletions") were independently re-derived from git show 5d6fe6f --stat (73 insertions/5 deletions across 5 files; subtracting the self-referential 8-line findings record gives exactly 65/5 across 4 tracked files) and are accurate. Item 5 of the audit brief (the two [design-open] items' exhaustiveness) checked clean for item 1 (reconciler fold-point: (a) absorb now vs (b) ship pre-pass first, successor row — a reasonable binary given the stated constraint) and is addressed by finding 4 for item 2 (RESERVED encoding — now moot, see finding 4's disposition).

WHY NOT PASS. Findings 1-4 are not cosmetic: finding 1 is the same class of coverage overclaim the S04 spec audit found in this project's history (findings/T584-s04-spec-audit.json finding 1) recurring in a sibling spec by a different sub-lead; findings 3 and 4 are self-contradictions within the same document, one caused by a same-day amendment the spec's own §2 acknowledges but §4/§10 do not, the other caused by an operator ruling that landed after the spec's citation pin but before this audit. All four are cheap to fix (table edits, not redesign) and none touch the sprint's actual architecture — the one-policy-file/one-dashboard/one-arbiter design is sound; it is the worked examples and the coverage claim that lag the ground truth by a few hours.

VERDICT: RATIFIABLE-WITH-AMENDMENTS. Ratify the architecture; require the rev-2 fixes for findings 1-4 (major) before P2 design begins, since P2 explicitly consumes §9's control table and §12's design-open list as inputs — shipping design work against the stale versions of either would need redoing.
